disagreements.label: valid

disagreements.label: valid
disagreements.why: The file contains END=0 on a record at POS 100 (END cannot precede POS) and, from 4.3, an SB value with one number where the reserved definition is Number=4.

disagreements.label: valid

disagreements.label: valid

disagreements.label: valid
disagreements.why: The file is empty (0 bytes). biolint reports an empty file as an error for every format (TXT010) because it nearly always means a failed step, and `samtools view` refuses it as well.
disagreements.first: TXT010 empty-file @0:0 the file is empty (0 bytes)

disagreements.label: valid
disagreements.why: A blank line splits the sequence of the second record. NCBI states that blank lines are not allowed in the middle of FASTA input and samtools faidx cannot index the file; the index entry itself notes that BioPerl, where the file comes from, considers it invalid.
disagreements.first: FA005 blank-line-in-sequence @17:0 1 blank line inside the sequence of `CEESC13F`

disagreements.label: valid
disagreements.why: Sequence lines contain pairs of spaces (the "cutpoints" of a BioRuby test) and three records reuse an earlier identifier. Spaces are not residue codes in the NCBI description and shift the coordinates of a faidx index, so biolint reports them as errors; some parsers strip them.
disagreements.first: FA010 sequence-whitespace @22:21 2 whitespace characters inside the sequence line

disagreements.label: valid
disagreements.why: The file has `#` comment lines before, between and after the records, a Biopython test of its own leniency (the file says "I don't really know if FASTA format is supposed to support this"). No description of FASTA has `#` comments, and samtools faidx stops at the first one.
disagreements.first: FA009 comment-line @1:1 comment line starting with `#`

disagreements.label: valid
disagreements.why: Ten of the fourteen records reuse an earlier identifier (`seq3`, `seq4`, ...). Parsers read the file, but an index keeps only the first record of that name (samtools faidx: "Ignoring duplicate sequence"), so biolint makes duplicate identifiers a warning by default and an error in the strict profile.
disagreements.first: FA008 duplicate-id @7:2 identifier `seq3` was already used on line 5

disagreements.label: valid
disagreements.why: `##gff-version 3` is on line 3, after two comment lines written by gffread; the specification requires it to be the topmost line. (The default profile accepts the file.)
disagreements.first: GFF003 version-not-first @3:1 `##gff-version` is on line 3, not on the first line

disagreements.label: invalid
disagreements.why: A thirteenth column after twelve valid BED fields is a custom field (BED12+1, §1.3 and §1.10). The corpus rejects it only because the directory expects exactly BED12, which the file itself cannot declare.

disagreements.label: invalid
disagreements.why: The line is a consistent BED12 feature followed by 22 further columns, which the specification allows as custom fields (BED12+22). The index gives no reason for the label, and the twelve standard fields break no rule.

disagreements.label: valid
disagreements.why: Chromosome names such as `NM_007524.1` contain a dot. The specimen was labelled against the UCSC description, which has no naming rule; BED v1.0 §1.5 restricts chrom to letters, digits and underscore. biolint accepts the file in its default profile.
disagreements.first: BED020 chrom-name @1:10 chrom `NM_007524.1` contains `.`; the specification allows only letters, digits and `_`
